tech_stack: C# / ASP.NET Core, SQL Server (EF Core), Redis, Apache Kafka (Avro / Seismic SharedEventBus)

http_deps: AuthService — OAuth2 token validation and certificate-based client auth
BlobStorageService — file uploads for bulk import/export
background_services: UMSEventConsumerBackgroundService — Kafka consumer host for all UMS events
SmartGroupJobService — evaluates dynamic membership rules on user change
BulkJobService — orchestrates bulk import/export via JMS
UserV1V2SyncService — migrates user data from V1 to V2 schema
GroupV1V2SyncService — migrates group data from V1 to V2 schema
RoleSyncService — syncs role and entitlement assignments

domains.name: User
domains.responsibility: Manages the full lifecycle of user identities within a tenant, including creation, deactivation, deletion, group membership, and V1-to-V2 schema migration.
domains.health_reason: User class (User.cs) has 30+ public settable properties and zero behavior methods; all business logic (deactivation guards, SSO-ID uniqueness, membership updates, cache invalidation, event publishing) lives in DefaultUserService, which has 16 constructor dependencies and ~2,200 lines.

invariants: SSO ID must be unique within a tenant
A deleted user cannot be reactivated
A deactivated user retains group memberships
IsLocked users cannot be modified by non-admin callers

domains.name: Group
domains.responsibility: Manages standard groups including membership, ownership, parent-child hierarchy relationships, and deactivation.
domains.health_reason: Group class (Group.cs) has 24 public settable properties and zero behavior methods; hierarchy validation, member management, cache invalidation, and event publishing all live in GroupService, which has 14 constructor dependencies.

invariants: Group name must be unique within a tenant
A group cannot be its own ancestor
EveryoneGroup cannot be deleted or deactivated
A deactivated group cannot accept new members

domains.name: Smart Group
domains.responsibility: Defines and evaluates dynamic membership rules that automatically include users matching configured field criteria.
domains.health_reason: SmartGroup rule model exists but evaluation logic is entirely in DefaultSmartGroupService and SmartGroupJobService; the aggregate has no method to evaluate or validate its own rules.
key_operations: SmartGroupJobService — async rule evaluation on user attribute change

invariants: Rule fields must reference valid custom property schemas
Smart group membership is computed-only; members cannot be manually added
A deactivated smart group stops evaluating rules

domains.name: Manager Hierarchy
domains.responsibility: Tracks manager-reportee reporting relationships and maintains hierarchy groups that mirror the live organisational tree.
domains.health_reason: Hierarchy logic is split across ManagerHierarchyService, HierarchyGroupService, and ManagerHierarchyJobService with no single aggregate encapsulating tree invariants; circular-relationship detection lives in service code.
key_operations: ManagerHierarchyMigrationController — sync and migrate hierarchy data

invariants: No circular reporting relationships allowed
A user may have at most one direct manager
Hierarchy groups must always mirror the live reporting tree

domains.name: Custom Property
domains.responsibility: Manages tenant-defined schema extensions for users and groups, including property type definitions, validation rules, and dropdown option lists.
domains.health_reason: CustomPropertyService and DataSchemaService have focused responsibilities; repository interfaces are well-defined and the schema/value separation is clear.

invariants: Property name must be unique within a tenant
Dropdown properties must have at least one option
A deprecated schema cannot accept new values

domains.name: Delegation
domains.responsibility: Manages temporary authority grants allowing one user to act on behalf of another within defined scopes and time windows.
domains.health_reason: Delegation lifecycle rules (expiry enforcement, scope validation, self-delegation guard) appear to live in DelegationService rather than a Delegation aggregate.

invariants: A user cannot delegate to themselves
Delegation period must have a defined end date
An expired delegation cannot be reactivated
Scope must reference valid permission identifiers

domains.name: Bulk Operation
domains.responsibility: Orchestrates asynchronous bulk import and export of users and groups via file-based jobs backed by blob storage and JMS.
domains.health_reason: BulkController directly calls IBlobStorageService and IJobManagementService (infrastructure), performs CSV writing in controller methods, and BulkJobService is a thin JMS wrapper with no domain logic; no BulkJob aggregate encapsulates job state transitions.

invariants: A completed or failed job cannot be retried without creating a new job
A cancelled job must release its blob storage reference
Results are immutable once the job reaches a terminal state

domains.name: SCIM Provisioning
domains.responsibility: Implements the SCIM 2.0 protocol adapter translating external identity-provider provisioning requests into internal User and Group domain operations.
domains.health_reason: SCIM controllers delegate to scimUserService/scimGroupService but the SCIM layer makes direct service calls without consistently routing through the User and Group domain aggregates; protocol translation and domain orchestration are mixed.
key_operations: SCIMUsersController — SCIM /Users CRUD and group membership

invariants: SCIM externalId must map to exactly one internal user or group
Patch operations must be applied atomically
SCIM responses must conform to RFC 7644 envelope structure

domains.name: User Sync Config
domains.responsibility: Manages configuration profiles for identity-provider synchronisation sources, defining attribute mappings, sync schedules, and saved query templates.
domains.health_reason: UserSyncConfigController, QueryStorageController, and EmailTemplateController are grouped under a single service boundary but manage loosely related concerns (IdP sync config, saved queries, email templates) that could be further separated.

invariants: A paused sync config will not process incoming IdP events
Attribute mappings must reference valid custom property schemas
A deleted sync config cannot be reactivated

domains.name: People Search
domains.responsibility: Provides unified cross-entity search across users and groups to support directory-style lookups, combined result sets, and saved query execution.
domains.health_reason: CombinedSearchService and PeopleService are query-only but fan out directly to multiple repositories without a read-model or CQRS projection; cache warm/invalidation is exposed as an API endpoint mixing operational concerns into the search domain.

invariants: A saved query must reference only valid property schema fields
Search results are always tenant-scoped and never cross tenant boundaries

steps.label: IdP sends SCIM POST /Users to SCIMUsersController
SCIMUsersController validates SCIM resource envelope
IScimUserService maps SeismicCore2EnterpriseUser to internal User model
DefaultUserService.CreateUserAsync enforces SSO-ID uniqueness and creates User
CustomPropertyService applies mapped attribute values
UmsEventBus.SendUserEvent publishes UserCreatedEvent to Kafka
UserEventConsumerForSmartGroup receives UserCreatedEvent
SmartGroupJobService evaluates all tenant smart group rules against new user
GroupMemberEvent published for each smart group membership gain
Client POSTs file to BulkController.UploadAsync
BulkController calls IBlobStorageService.UploadAsync directly (infra in controller)
BulkController calls IBulkJobService.CreateImportBulkJobAsync
BulkJobService calls IJobManagementService.CreateBulkImportJobAsync (infra in service)
JMS executes job asynchronously in Executor layer
BulkJobService processes each row via DefaultUserService.CreateUserAsync or UpdateUserAsync
GroupService.AddMemberAsync updates group memberships per row
CustomPropertyService applies property values per row
BulkJobCompletedEvent published to Kafka on terminal state
ManagerHierarchyMigrationController triggers rebuild via POST
ManagerHierarchyJobService queues async subtree rebuild via JMS
ManagerHierarchyService traverses user manager fields to compute tree
HierarchyGroupService updates HierarchyGroup entities to mirror new tree
UserSyncResultEvent published to Kafka with batch membership changes
UserEventConsumer processes downstream group membership side-effects
UserEvent consumed by UserEventConsumerForSmartGroup
SmartGroupJobService identifies all smart groups affected by changed user attributes
DefaultSmartGroupService evaluates each rule set against updated user
Membership delta (adds and removes) computed
GroupMemberEvent published per membership change
GroupEventConsumer updates denormalised group membership data

UserV1V2SyncService reads LibraryUser (V1) rows in batches
V1 fields mapped to LibraryUserV2 schema
LaunchDarkly flag gates V2 read path activation per tenant
UserEventConsumerForV1ToV2Sync keeps V2 in sync with live V1 writes
UserEventConsumerForV2ToV1Sync back-propagates V2 changes to V1 during dual-write period

gap_analysis.title: Anemic User aggregate
gap_analysis.detail: User.cs contains 30+ public settable properties and zero behavior methods. Business rules such as deactivation guards (a deleted user cannot be reactivated), SSO-ID uniqueness enforcement, group membership limits, and lock checks all live in DefaultUserService. This means invariants are scattered and can be bypassed by any caller that constructs a User directly.

gap_analysis.title: Anemic Group aggregate
gap_analysis.detail: Group.cs contains 24 public settable properties and zero behavior methods. Hierarchy cycle detection, EveryoneGroup protection, and member management logic all live in GroupService. The aggregate cannot protect its own invariants.

gap_analysis.title: DefaultUserService god object — 16 dependencies
gap_analysis.detail: DefaultUserService constructor takes 16 injected dependencies (IGroupRepository, IUserRepository, IUserIdentifyValidator, ICustomPropertyService, IDataSchemaService, ICustomPropertyVerifyService, ILibraryCacheNotitionSevice, IRequestContext, IUmsEventBus, ILogger, UmsDeployInfo, IUserCacheService, IHttpContextAccessor, IUserPostChangeProcessor, IGroupInterceptor, IGroupMemberEventService) and spans ~2,200 lines. It mixes CRUD, validation, cache management, event publishing, HTTP context inspection, and feature flag evaluation in a single class.

gap_analysis.title: Infrastructure calls directly in BulkController
gap_analysis.detail: BulkController injects IBlobStorageService and IJobManagementService and calls them directly in action methods: UploadAsync calls BlobStorageService.UploadAsync(), GetDownloadFileAsync calls BlobStorageService.GetDownloadUrlAsync(), GetExceptionDownloadFileAsync calls BlobStorageService.UploadAsync() and writes CSV bytes inline. Controllers should delegate to application services; infrastructure must not be called from the HTTP layer.

gap_analysis.title: Domain events modelled as Kafka infrastructure events
gap_analysis.detail: UserEvent, GroupEvent, GroupMemberEvent, and UserCustomPropertyEvent are Avro-serialised Kafka message classes living in the infrastructure layer. There is no domain event abstraction (e.g. IDomainEvent). Business logic raises events by calling IUmsEventBus directly rather than appending to an aggregate's domain event list, coupling the domain layer to the messaging infrastructure.

gap_analysis.title: GroupService god object — 14 dependencies
gap_analysis.detail: GroupService constructor takes 14 injected dependencies and directly calls ICacheService.InvalidateAsync(), IUmsEventBus.SendGroupEvent(), IGroupRepository, and IGroupV2OwnerRepository inside business methods. Validation, persistence, caching, and event publishing are collapsed into a single service.

gap_analysis.title: SCIM layer bypasses User/Group domain layer
gap_analysis.detail: SCIMUsersController injects IScimUserService and ISCIMGroupService which make direct repository calls rather than routing through DefaultUserService and GroupService. This means SCIM provisioning bypasses domain invariants (e.g. SSO-ID uniqueness, EveryoneGroup protection) enforced only in the core services.

gap_analysis.title: LaunchDarkly feature flag evaluated inside domain service
gap_analysis.detail: DefaultUserService calls LaunchDarklyHelper.EnableRepoV2() inside business methods to choose between LibraryUser and LibraryUserV2 repositories. Feature flag infrastructure does not belong in the domain layer; this should be resolved at the application or composition root layer before reaching the service.

gap_analysis.title: BulkJobService is a thin JMS wrapper with no domain logic
gap_analysis.detail: BulkJobService contains two lines of logic per method — all delegating directly to IJobManagementService. The BulkJob lifecycle (Queued → Processing → Completed/Failed/Cancelled) has no aggregate representation; state transitions are entirely implicit in JMS.

gap_analysis.title: HTTP context inspected inside DefaultUserService
gap_analysis.detail: DefaultUserService accesses IHttpContextAccessor.HttpContext.Request.Headers inside business methods to extract caller context. Domain services must not depend on HTTP infrastructure; caller identity should be passed as a typed parameter from the application layer.

gap_analysis.title: V1/V2 dual-write complexity with bidirectional sync consumers
gap_analysis.detail: UserEventConsumerForV1ToV2Sync and UserEventConsumerForV2ToV1Sync maintain bidirectional synchronisation between LibraryUser and LibraryUserV2. This creates a potential event loop, complicates debugging, and doubles the surface area for data inconsistency. A migration completion date and V1 deprecation plan should be established to eliminate the dual-write path.

gap_analysis.title: No read model for People Search — direct multi-repository fan-out
gap_analysis.detail: CombinedSearchService and PeopleService fan out to IUserRepository and IGroupRepository directly with no CQRS read projection or materialised view. Queries cross the User and Group domain boundaries without a dedicated query model, making performance tuning and search relevance improvements difficult.

gap_analysis.title: Repository interface fragmentation
gap_analysis.detail: The codebase defines IUserRepository, IBulkUserRepository, IThinUserRepository, IUserCacheService, IGroupRepository, IGroupV2OwnerRepository, and more. The proliferation of narrow repository interfaces without a query specification pattern leads to duplicate method signatures and makes it hard to understand the full query surface of each aggregate.

gap_analysis.title: Controllers return domain model objects directly
gap_analysis.detail: Several controllers return User and Group domain objects (or collections thereof) directly via IActionResult without mapping to response DTOs. This couples the API contract to the internal domain model, making non-breaking API evolution harder and leaking internal fields (e.g. LegacyId, DirectManagedGroupLegacyIds) to external consumers.
